messages:
Maria (eng-runtime): Heads up — we started getting intermittent 404s for the model-serving path in us-west-2-edge-3 around 10:12 UTC. Only affects the headless svc `mymodel-gpu-svc` backing the GPU pods. Can anyone eyeball CoreDNS/kube-proxy?
Sam (sre): Is the error DNS-level or routing? Any logs/`kubectl` output you can paste?
Maria (eng-runtime): Quick dumps: `kubectl -n models get svc mymodel-gpu-svc -o yaml` shows `clusterIP: None` (headless). `kubectl -n models get endpointslices` shows the number of EndpointSlices flapping — sometimes 0 entries for that svc. CoreDNS logs include repeats of: `kubernetes: no endpoints found for service "mymodel-gpu-svc"`
Alex (infra): Paste of coredns excerpt: `[ERROR] kubernetes: failed to get endpoints for service "mymodel-gpu-svc": endpoints not found` — saw that too. Any kube-proxy errors on nodes?
Maria (eng-runtime): Pulled kube-proxy log from node-7: `E0323 10:13:14 proxier.go:198] failed to sync iptables: could not ensure chains: conntrack table full` and `iptables: failed to write chain` in repeated bursts. conntrack usage: `ss -s` shows ~920k entries on nodes where requests failed (sysctl nf_conntrack_max=1M).
Jin (platform): If conntrack is saturated, kube-proxy fails to program rules and traffic to pod IPs can drop even though pods are Running. That plus EndpointSlice churn could make CoreDNS look like there are no endpoints.
Sam (sre): Agrees — the symptoms match: endpoint slice controller creating/deleting slices rapidly -> coredns receives transient no-endpoint responses; cache plugin then returns negative answers for some TTL causing clients to see 404/NXDOMAIN for a short window.
Maria (eng-runtime): Repro commands I ran: ```
# on control plane
kubectl -n models get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=mymodel-gpu-svc -o wide
# on node
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
ss -s | grep conntrack
```
Alex (infra): Proposed mitigation steps (canary): 1) bump node conntrack (`sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=5242880`) 2) restart kube-proxy on canary node(s) so it reprograms rules (or cordon/drain + uncordon) 3) restart coredns pods to clear negative cache 4) delete stale EndpointSlices for the svc to force rebuild.
Sam (sre): I'm going to run the canary on node-7/8 now. Plan: bump nf_conntrack_max, cordon & drain node-7, restart kube-proxy ds pod on that node, restart coredns deployment in kube-system after proxier is healthy, then uncordon.
ops-bot: kube-proxy DaemonSet restart scheduled on node-7 by @sam (sre) — 10:21 UTC
Sam (sre): Ran the steps on node-7: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=5242880`. After kube-proxy pod restart, proxier logs no longer show conntrack full errors. EndpointSlice count stabilized for the svc.
Maria (eng-runtime): Restarted coredns (`kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns`) — negative cache cleared, DNS answers now return pod IPs for headless svc. Client 404 rate dropped to near zero.
Alex (infra): Root cause hypothesis: high endpoint churn (GPU pod restarts/evictions during warmup) created EndpointSlice update storms. Kube-proxy hit conntrack capacity and couldn't program iptables rules, causing packets to drop. CoreDNS saw transient no-endpoints and the cache plugin returned negative answers for TTL window → manifesting as short 404/NXDOMAIN windows for clients.
Jin (platform): Action items agreed: 1) Add alert for node conntrack usage and kube-proxy sync errors (threshold: 80% conntrack usage / any proxier sync failures). 2) Triage ways to reduce endpoint churn (graceful termination, backoff on pod churn for model warmups). 3) Evaluate switching kube-proxy mode to ipvs on edge fleet where churn is high. 4) Tune CoreDNS cache negative TTL for headless service patterns or disable negative caching for service lookups.
Maria (eng-runtime): I'll open a postmortem ticket with timeline and add the immediate remediation steps we ran to the runbook.
Sam (sre): FYI — rolling change: we'll roll the conntrack bump to the rest of the edge nodes tonight during off-peak and schedule ipvs migration R&D next sprint. :thumbsup:
Alex (infra): Also adding a short-term script to detect EndpointSlice update rate spikes and write an event if > X updates/min for the same svc. Might help catch regressions early.
Maria (eng-runtime): Great — thanks everyone. Follow-up ticket: INF-2318.
Sam (sre): Closing this thread — reopen if we see reoccurence.
